tools.name: spark_save_job
tools.description: Save a syntactically valid UTF-8 PySpark application.

tools.name: spark_read_job
tools.description: Read a bounded saved PySpark application before making a targeted repair.

tools.name: spark_replace_job_text
tools.description: Replace exact text in one saved job and reject ambiguous or invalid repairs.

tools.name: spark_validate_job
tools.description: Parse a saved Spark job and report whether it imports PySpark.

tools.name: spark_submit_job
tools.description:
Submit one immutable snapshot with single-process persistent replay safety.

    HDFS arguments must use the physical path returned by an HDFS tool, for example
    ``/mcp/lab/input.log``, or the equivalent full URI
    ``hdfs://namenode:9000/mcp/lab/input.log``. Never pass an HDFS MCP virtual path
    such as ``/lab/input.log`` to Spark.

    An idempotency key requires the trusted caller's expected code hash. Durable
    reservations make replays safe across restarts, but the asyncio lock does not
    coordinate multiple MCP server replicas. Snapshots and terminal state are
    intentionally retained for audit.

tools.name: spark_job_status
tools.description: Return durable status for a submitted job.

tools.name: spark_job_logs
tools.description: Return combined stdout/stderr from a submitted job.

tools.name: spark_cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a running Spark job submitted by this server process.

tools.name: spark_list_jobs
tools.description: List recent MCP-submitted jobs.

tools.name: spark_cluster_status
tools.description: Return Spark master capacity, applications, and registered workers.

tools.name: hdfs_list

tools.name: hdfs_stat
tools.description: Get metadata by virtual path below /mcp; do not include the /mcp prefix.

tools.name: hdfs_mkdir
tools.description: Create by virtual path below /mcp; the result returns its physical path.

tools.name: hdfs_write_text
tools.description: Write by virtual path below /mcp; the result returns its physical path.

tools.name: hdfs_read_text
tools.description: Read by virtual path below /mcp; do not include the /mcp prefix.

tools.name: hdfs_delete
tools.description: Delete by virtual path below /mcp; deleting the root itself is forbidden.

tools.name: hdfs_import_file
tools.description:
Verify a stable import in HDFS before publishing it with an atomic rename.

    ``destination`` is an HDFS MCP virtual path such as ``/lab/input.log``; do not
    include the ``/mcp`` prefix. The returned ``destination`` is the physical HDFS
    path, such as ``/mcp/lab/input.log``. Pass that returned value unchanged to
    PySpark or ``spark_submit_job``. Do not pass it back into an HDFS MCP tool.

    Callers must serialize writes to one destination. An existing destination is
    replay-safe when ``overwrite`` is false and its exact bytes already match the
    stable source. Otherwise an existing destination is moved to a temporary
    backup for rollback because FsShell rename does not provide a cross-replica
    compare-and-swap operation.

tools.name: hdfs_cluster_status
tools.description: Return HDFS capacity, block health, and DataNode counts.

tools.name: hdfs_sha256
tools.description: Stream the whole real HDFS file (text or binary) and return its SHA-256. Virtual path omits /mcp.

tools.name: hdfs_read_lines
tools.description: Read numbered UTF-8 records without loading a large log into model context. Lines are one-based; returns next_line.

tools.name: hdfs_query_records
tools.description: Scan an entire JSONL or key=value log. Exact filters are AND across fields, OR within each list (values compared as strings). Field names are literal, including dots. Return counts, sums, distinct counts, UTC time/interval statistics and original line references. No attack labels or hidden detection rules. Missing requested fields fail rather than becoming zero. time_field must contain epoch seconds or timezone-aware ISO text; omit for split date/time fields.

tools.name: hdfs_correlate_records
tools.description: Join two real HDFS log views by equal keys AND timestamp tolerance. Use UID/parentuid or a full directional tuple (source/dest IP, source/dest port, protocol). Literal field names. Time fields: one epoch/ISO field, or two date/time fields; timezone-less input requires explicit naive_timezone='UTC'. Return full-source hashes, line-numbered pairs, deltas, unmatched counts and one-to-many cardinality. Counts are records/pairs, not automatically sessions. Optional left_group_by returns exact matched cohort counts and first/last left timestamps (up to 100 groups). No attack verdict.

tools.name: hdfs_pcap_packets
tools.description: Inspect a real HDFS PCAP using TShark/Wireshark display-filter syntax. Scans the capture and returns matching packet count plus bounded numbered packet evidence and TCP payload hex/text. Use numeric addresses; name resolution is disabled. Packet count is not connection count. Requires tshark installed in the MCP image.
